criteria.title: Transient dead letters re-run exactly at the 1h, 4h, and 16h boundaries (time hacked by backdating)
criteria.plain: A transient dead letter is re-run once about an hour after it died, again about four hours after the next death, and again after sixteen; one that is a minute short of each boundary is left alone.
criteria.doIt: Seed six transient dead letters with backdated death times (61m/59m at requeues 0, 4h01/3h59 at requeues 1, 16h01/15h59 at requeues 2), run the worker binary for 30s with the reaper ticking every 5s, read the six rows.
criteria.expectIt: The three 'due' rows have requeues incremented by one and requeued_at set; the three 'short' rows are unchanged (same requeues, requeued_at NULL, status dead_letter).

source.ref: Task 4 Interfaces: interval requeue 1h x 4^requeues, requeues < 3

proof.detail: the six groups are titled with the run marker and returned with their counters

args: SELECT g.title, j.status, j.requeues, j.requeued_at IS NOT NULL AS requeued FROM error_group_jobs j JOIN error_groups g ON g.id = j.error_group_id WHERE g.title LIKE 'AC1 {{marker}} %' ORDER BY g.title

criteria.title: A repository the worker cannot clone is still a needs_human incident with repo_access_denied
criteria.plain: With a real sandbox but no GitHub credential, a private repository cannot be cloned, and the incident lands in needs_human for the customer with the repo_access_denied reason.
criteria.doIt: Wait for the seeded job on the private <private-repo> project, run the worker binary for 200s with real E2B and model keys but GITHUB_TOKEN unset, read the group and job.
criteria.expectIt: Group status needs_human, reason_code repo_access_denied, needs_human_at set; job completed (not dead-lettered), attempts 0.

source.ref: Decisions: needs_human is reserved for things the customer must act on, including a repository the worker cannot access

proof.detail: the group is titled with the run marker and returned with its terminal fields

args: SELECT count(*) FROM error_group_jobs j LEFT JOIN error_groups g ON g.id = j.error_group_id WHERE g.title = 'AC2 {{marker}}' AND j.available_at <= now()

SELECT g.title, g.status, g.reason_code, g.needs_human_at IS NOT NULL AS has_needs_human_at, j.status AS job_status, j.attempts, j.dead_letter_class, left(j.last_error, 100) AS last_error FROM error_groups g JOIN error_group_jobs j ON j.error_group_id = g.id WHERE g.title = 'AC2 {{marker}}'

criteria.title: A real investigation capped at one turn ends in one execution, labelled limit or agent, with the incident still in analyzing
criteria.plain: When the model runs out of room on a real investigation of a real repository, the job is not retried, the incident is not shown to the customer, and the failure is labelled as ours.
criteria.doIt: Wait for the seeded job, run the worker binary for 300s with real E2B, model, and GitHub credentials and FRICTION_INVESTIGATION_MAX_TURNS=1, read the group and job.
criteria.expectIt: Either group awaiting_approval with a verdict, or: job dead_letter, attempts 1, dead_letter_class limit or agent, group analyzing, reason_code NULL. The worker output has no 'Friction investigation API call failed' line and no 'retry the job'. Report which class was observed.

proof.detail: the group title carries the marker and is read with the job row after the run

args: SELECT count(*) FROM error_group_jobs j LEFT JOIN error_groups g ON g.id = j.error_group_id WHERE g.title = 'AC3 {{marker}}' AND j.available_at <= now()

SELECT g.title, g.status, g.reason_code, j.status AS job_status, j.attempts, j.dead_letter_class, j.requeues, left(j.last_error, 120) AS last_error FROM error_groups g JOIN error_group_jobs j ON j.error_group_id = g.id WHERE g.title = 'AC3 {{marker}}'

criteria.title: A provider outage retries through the queue and never becomes a customer verdict
criteria.plain: If the model provider answers 529 to every call, the job is retried with backoff and finally dead-lettered as transient; the incident is never written to the customer as an evidence verdict.
criteria.doIt: Wait for the seeded job, run the worker binary for 480s with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointing at a local stub that always answers 529 (real E2B and GitHub credentials), read the job and group.
criteria.expectIt: attempts >= 2 within the window (3 and status dead_letter with dead_letter_class transient if the provider retries fit); the group is analyzing with reason_code NULL and no decision row written; last_error names the 529 or 'model unavailable'.

source.ref: Task 2 steps 3 and 5: transient failures use the queue's backoff; no insufficient_context or unable_to_establish_cause write

proof.detail: the group title carries the marker and is read with the job row after the run

args: SELECT count(*) FROM error_group_jobs j LEFT JOIN error_groups g ON g.id = j.error_group_id WHERE g.title = 'AC4 {{marker}}' AND j.available_at <= now()

SELECT g.title, g.status, g.reason_code, j.status AS job_status, j.attempts, j.dead_letter_class, left(j.last_error, 120) AS last_error, (SELECT count(*) FROM diagnosis_decisions dd WHERE dd.error_group_id = g.id) AS decisions FROM error_groups g JOIN error_group_jobs j ON j.error_group_id = g.id WHERE g.title = 'AC4 {{marker}}'

criteria.title: The route classifier completes on a real Vue repository and writes one route_map row per discovered route
criteria.plain: The daily route map for a real app finishes within its (route-scaled) budget instead of dying, and every discovered route gets a row.
criteria.doIt: Wait for the seeded route_map job for the papermark project, run the worker binary for 480s with real credentials, read the job and the route_map rows, compare against the independently listed page files.
criteria.expectIt: Job completed (not dead_letter). route_map rows for project ...0020 number between 40 and 120, against 80 page files (7 app-router page.tsx plus pages/*.tsx excluding api, _app, _document) listed independently in expected-routes.txt; the worker's 'Product context persisted' line agrees with the row count. A count of 0 or 1, or a dead letter on budget, fails.

proof.detail: route_map rows and the job status are read after the run; the worker's persisted-count log line is in the run output

args: SELECT count(*) FROM error_group_jobs j LEFT JOIN error_groups g ON g.id = j.error_group_id WHERE j.job_type = 'route_map' AND j.project_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000020' AND j.available_at <= now()

SELECT j.job_type, j.status, j.attempts, j.dead_letter_class, left(j.last_error, 120) AS last_error, (SELECT count(*) FROM route_map rm WHERE rm.project_id = j.project_id) AS route_rows FROM error_group_jobs j WHERE j.job_type = 'route_map' AND j.project_id = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000020'
